source: # The escape codec, in both directions.
#   source   a cell exactly as it appears in a fixture file (raw).
#   value    JSON of unescape(source) — the string a parser would receive.
#   escaped  JSON of escape(value) — the canonical way to write it back.
# `value` and `escaped` are JSON because the decoded text contains the
# very characters a TSV cell cannot hold; JSON's own escapes carry them.
# Where `source` is already canonical, `escaped` decodes back to it.
# `\\n` is an escaped backslash followed by a literal n — NOT a newline.
# Decoding left to right is what keeps those two apart.
# An unrecognised escape passes through untouched, so a fixture can carry
# its own backslashes (a regex, a JSON escape, a Windows path) unquoted.
# A lone trailing backslash has nothing to escape and stays as it is.
